feature: Type a key's value beside the key
summary: Clicking any key on a property's row, or a point on its graph, opens a small popover just above it showing that value at the key, ready to type, with Reset. The canvas shows the new value at once.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. A title on a recording with Opacity keyed at two moments (Animate a property, Opacity, then Key at a second moment).

try.do: Open the title's track and click the Opacity key at the later moment.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the Opacity number in the popover, type 40 and press Return.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Shift-click the other Opacity key, type 70 in the popover and press Return.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Escape, click Graph in the panel's Animating header, then click the point at the later moment.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Animate the title's Color, click its key, then click the swatch in the popover.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick another tool, or click anywhere off the popover.

evaluate: Does the popover open where your eye already is, just above the key, without hiding the key?
Is typing a key's value here quicker than finding the same number in the panel?
With two keys picked, is 'Mixed %' clear, and does one typed number setting both feel right?
Does the popover read as the same family as the transform values popover from the tool bar's Info button?
When it sits over the clip bar of the row above, is that acceptable, or should it prefer another side?
rough: The mock draws a one-line bar; this is the vertical popover with name left and value right, as the placement rule says (UX-PATTERNS 'Named exception: the transform values', your call on 2026-10-13).
A diamond on the clip's own bar only picks its keys and opens no popover: the mock sent that click to the canvas bar you replaced with the Info popover (your call on 2026-10-13).
Reset puts Position in the middle of the canvas, as the mock does; a colour or a text size has no default, so Reset is dimmed for those keys. No mock covers the colour case beyond the swatch and hex.
Above a key on the first row the popover sits over the timeline ruler and the clip bar above; it never covers the key itself.
The playhead's line shows softly through the popover's glass where it passes behind it; the text stays readable.
